t: Such sums as may be deposited to the Medical Care Collections Fund pursuant to section 1729A of title 38, United States Code, for healthcare provided at facilities designated as combined Federal medical facilities as described by section 706 of the Duncan Hunter National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2009 (Public Law 110–417; 122 Stat. 4500) shall also be available: (1) for transfer to the Joint Department of Defense-Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Facility Demonstration Fund, established by section 1704 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2010 (Public Law 111–84; 123 Stat. 3571); and (2) for operations of the facilities designated as combined Federal medical facilities as described by section 706 of the Duncan Hunter National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2009 (Public Law 110–417; 122 Stat. 4500).

fable.w: This is an appropriations provision making deposited funds available for transfer to a joint DoD-VA fund and for operating combined federal medical facilities. The tempting reading is that the "Joint" DoD-VA arrangement implies coordination, but that is purely between federal agencies and involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, or right to sue for any outside party. No one outside the federal government is brought into any federal decision.
fable.s: shall also be available: (1) for transfer to the Joint Department of Defense-Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Facility Demonstration Fund

qwen_block.w: This section is an appropriations provision that authorizes the transfer and use of federal funds between government entities (the Medical Care Collections Fund, the Joint DoD-VA Fund, and combined Federal medical facilities). It does not involve consultation, coordination, or participation with any parties outside the federal government, such as states, tribes, the public, or private organizations.
qwen_block.s: Such sums as may be deposited to the Medical Care Collections Fund... shall also be available: (1) for transfer to the Joint Department of Defense-Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Facility Demonstration Fund... and (2) for operations of the facilities designated as combined Federal medical facilities

opus.w: This is an appropriations provision. It makes money deposited in the Medical Care Collections Fund available for transfer to a joint fund and for running combined federal medical facilities. The only actors are federal departments (DoD and VA), so any 'joint' or 'combined' arrangement is coordination inside the government. No state, tribe, expert, company or member of the public is consulted or given a role in any decision.
opus.s: shall also be available: (1) for transfer to the Joint Department of Defense-Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Facility Demonstration Fund
opus.b: **Tempting reading:** The words "Joint Department of Defense-Department of Veterans Affairs" and "combined Federal medical facilities" suggest coordination. But that coordination is only between two federal departments, and the provision is really just about which purposes the money can be used for.

qwen_chat.w: This section authorizes the transfer and use of federal funds between federal accounts and for the operation of federal facilities. It does not require or recommend consultation, coordination, or input from any party outside the federal government (such as the public, states, or private entities). All actors mentioned (Department of Defense, Department of Veterans Affairs, Congress) are inside the federal government.
qwen_chat.s: Such sums as may be deposited to the Medical Care Collections Fund... shall also be available: (1) for transfer to the Joint Department of Defense-Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Facility Demonstration Fund... and (2) for operations of the facilities designated as combined Federal medical facilities
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "combined Federal medical facilities" imply some form of partnership or coordination with outside entities (like state hospitals or private providers) that could constitute participation. However, the text strictly limits the discussion to the movement of funds between federal accounts ("Medical Care Collections Fund" and "Joint Department of Defense-Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Facility Demonstration Fund") and the operation of facilities designated as federal. There is no mention of consulting with, coordinating with, or allowing input from non-federal parties (such as the public, states, or private companies) in the decision-making process regarding these funds or facilities. The actors involved are entirely within the federal government (DoD, VA, Congress via appropriations).
